newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend rebound to fourth session.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend rebound to fourth session.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks extended their rally into a fourth session Thursday as some investors appeared more confident that the market was in legitimate recovery after its month-long selloff.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 27.70 points at 6,707.57. Since Monday the blue-chip index has recovered more than 40 percent of its 700-point plunge between March 11 and April 11.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 13-8 on New York Stock Exchange volume of 290 million shares.
The market's rally was in some ways more convincing as there was broader participation, including a solid showing by high technology shares, which have been weak for the last two days.
The Nasdaq Composite Index, which is laced with technology stocks, was up 12.89 points at 1,223.16.

The rise in bond market also buoyed sentiment. The 30-year Treasury bond rose 20/32, lowering its yield to 7.05 percent from Wednesday's close of 7.10 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
But analysts pointed out that the biggest stock market moves have been coming in the last hour, or even 30 minutes, when computerized programmes kick in.
"Today's rally is broader based. Techs are participating, and overall, the rally shows the market has resilience," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research.
"I do not expect to see the market keep moving higher. We are still vulnerable to another drop," Solloway said.
"But as long as the fundamentals are in good shape, and they certainly are, we should not see a sharper bear market type of decline," he said.
Solloway said some technology stocks, particularly networking companies and computer-makers like Compaq Computer Corp. were attractive and showing considerable strength.
"There is a demand for these products that will not go away," Solloway said. "There is great potential in foreign markets, particularly Europe."
Compaq, which Wednesday reported a two-thirds rise in profits, was up 1-5/8 at 75.
Intel Corp. was up 2-3/4 at 136-3/4. Cisco Systems Inc. rose 2 to 49-1/2. Microsoft Corp. was up 7/9 at 99-1/8 and International Business Machines Corp. was up 1-1/2 at 139.

ESS Technology Inc. dropped 8-3/16 to 13-7/8 in active trading after it warned that price pressure in the audio and video markets was expected to result in slimmer profit margins in the second quarter.
Among special situations, Cyrix Corp. jumped 3-57/62 to 21-41/62 after the computer chip maker reported first quarter net income that far surpassed Wall Street expectations.
